faults.fault: false claim at part of the range
faults.finding: 'The series part adds flux, so each amp gives more torque than in a shunt motor' is untrue below rated current: on the picture's rule the cumulative flux is 0.85 + 0.15 Ia, less than the shunt motor's 1.00 when Ia < 1.
faults.fix: 'The series part adds flux, so the torque climbs faster than the current.' True at every current on the rule.

faults.where: explain para 2, screen 3 right feedback, analogy
faults.finding: 'the flux cannot fall towards nothing', 'the flux never falls towards nothing' and 'it never over-revs' hold only while the shunt field is connected, and screen 6 itself shows the open-shunt case.
faults.fix: 'Here the shunt part keeps the flux up.' 'The shunt part stays, so the flux holds up.' Analogy: 'when the load comes off, it tops out instead of over-revving.'

faults.fault: interactive brief shows only the effect
faults.finding: The brief names the no-load speed and the starting torque but not the flux that causes both, though the picture draws two flux bars.
faults.fix: 'The one thing you should see is the light-load flux fall and the no-load speed climb towards the series motor's, while the heavy-current flux and torque rise, when you slide the series share up.'

faults.finding: It jumps to 'Speed = (1 − 0.0025) ÷ (0.95 × 0.8575)' without stating the speed rule, and the line hides the 0.9975 ÷ 0.95 = 1.05 step.
About 108 words; 'More than a shunt motor gives, less than a series motor' also reads badly, and the explain already gives the reason for the starting torque.

passed: the causal step: flux = steady shunt part + series part that grows with current; heavy load, more flux, torque climbs faster than current; load off, series part fades, shunt part stays, so a definite no-load speed; the series motor's whole-field fade named as the physical difference

the interactive shows the cause: two flux bars (light and heavy current) move with the share; settings where the effect is absent (0%, the shunt line) and extreme (100%, the series line runs away); the differential switch shows the speed rising with load

checks test the cause and a fault to find, each wrong option a named slip with its own reason: load off (runs away = series slip; hardly changes = shunt slip); speed rises with load after a rewind (open shunt = would slow with load; worn brushes = sparking, not speed)
